clue.text: Measure put through upper chamber

indicators.note: the measure is put through, running across the words that follow

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill is pushed through the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper chamber' reads as the House of Lords, but the answer runs across those two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch is an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a rod or pole.

clue.text: Small tablet slipped into large amount of pale ale is easy to swallow

indicators.note: the tablet is slipped inside the drink's letters
a large amount, but not all, so one letter is dropped from the drink

parts.note: taken as written
a tab is a small tablet or pill

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a pill into a big glass of beer to help it go down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large amount of' means most but not all, so one E goes from the beer, leaving PALALE before the pill slips in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palatable is pleasant to taste, agreeable enough to go down well.

clue.text: Notes top ten recording (new version)

indicators.note: in a down entry, to top something is to sit above it, so the notes come before the next piece

parts.note: re and mi are the second and third notes of the sol-fa scale
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A song tops the chart in a newly made version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top ten' suggests the charts; 'top' says RE MI sits above X in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A remix is a fresh version of a recorded track, with its parts rebalanced or reworked.

clue.text: Sycophant's number is up after executioner appears

indicators.note: after puts the next piece behind the executioner

parts.note: a hanger is one who hangs, an executioner

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the number word is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A flatterer's time is up when the hangman arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number is up' sounds like doom; 'is up' turns NO to ON. 'Appears' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a toady who attaches themselves to someone for advantage.

clue.text: European films — they cause controversy

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
a film is a thin haze, and mists are thin hazes

explanation.surface: European cinema is said to provoke arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' suggests cinema; here it means thin coatings or hazes, as in a film of mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemists are people who write or speak in fierce argument, stirring up dispute.

clue.text: Stop advertisement for some tobacco

definitions.meaning: to block up a hole, as with a stopper
a cake or piece of pressed chewing tobacco

explanation.definitionFit: A plug stops a hole; plugging a product is promoting it; a plug of tobacco is a compressed chunk.

clue.text: Young man awfully likely to take lead in romance

definitions.text: Young man awfully likely to take lead in romance

parts.note: a lad is a young man

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of likely are messed up
the lead in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A young fellow who seems bound to lead in matters of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges LIKELY to YKILLE; 'lead in' takes R from 'romance'. The whole clue describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladykiller is a charming man who seduces women easily.

clue.text: Something of significance for a short time

definitions.meaning: importance, weight, as in 'of great consequence'

explanation.surface: Something important for just a brief while.
explanation.definitionFit: Moment means importance ('of great moment') and also an instant.

clue.text: Motor seat replaced, providing space for traveller

indicators.note: replaced suggests the letters are put back in a different place

explanation.surface: A car seat has been changed so a passenger has room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replaced' rearranges MOTORSEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stateroom is a private cabin on a ship or a train compartment.

clue.text: Quickly look at page and cut corners

parts.note: to skim is to read over quickly

explanation.surface: Glancing over a page and taking shortcuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise meanly, doing a job with too little effort or material.

clue.text: Scoundrel'"exposed in abridged foreign newspaper spread

indicators.note: the scoundrel is shown up inside the shortened paper, so his letters go within it
abridged means shortened, so the paper's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Le Monde is the leading French daily paper
a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue is unmasked in a cut-down French paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abridged' cuts LE MONDE to LEMOND, and 'exposed in' puts CUR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon curd is a sweet preserve made with lemons, eggs and butter, eaten spread on bread.

clue.text: Motorway doubled round a US city

indicators.note: round says the doubled letters go around the next piece
doubled says the motorway's letters appear twice in a row

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A motorway runs twice round an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubled' gives MIMI, and 'round' puts it around A. The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a large city in Florida, in the United States.

clue.text: Outward-bound American chopper proceeded down runway

indicators.note: outward says the tied-up word stands outside the next piece, wrapping it

parts.note: bound means tied, as with rope
ax is the American spelling of axe, a chopper

explanation.surface: An American helicopter heading abroad rolled along the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outward-bound' looks like one word for leaving; split it so 'Outward' wraps 'bound' around the axe. 'Chopper' wants to be a helicopter, which fits the runway picture, but here it is an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft taxies when it moves slowly along the ground before take-off or after landing.

clue.text: Superficial sort involved in leak

indicators.note: involved in places the kind inside the leak

parts.note: to leak is to seep out
a sort is a kind or type

explanation.surface: A shallow person gets caught up in a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' looks like a person (a superficial sort); it is the noun meaning type.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only on the outer layer, not going deep, is skin-deep, as in 'beauty is only skin-deep'.

clue.text: Like tarnished goods needing polished so badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are poorly arranged and need sorting

explanation.surface: Dull merchandise needs a really poor polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges POLISHEDSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled stock is dirty or faded from display in a store.

clue.text: Collar is part of a shirt

definitions.meaning: to collar someone is to stop and detain them to talk
the slit that takes a button on a shirt front or cuff

explanation.surface: A collar is said to be one piece of a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' reads as the shirt neckband; it is the verb meaning to waylay someone for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole is to accost and detain; a buttonhole is also the slit a button goes through.

clue.text: Dog food that might come off the back of a lorry?

definitions.text: that might come off the back of a lorry?

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them
board means meals, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Pet food that has suspiciously fallen off a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell off the back of a lorry' is British slang for stolen goods, but here the hinged back panel of a lorry is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailboard is the hinged, removable rear flap of a truck.

clue.text: Extinct bird born in ancient kingdom

parts.note: the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct
b is the abbreviation for born, as in biographies

explanation.surface: A vanished bird is said to have hatched in an old realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Moab was a kingdom east of the Dead Sea in biblical times.

clue.text: Tree, say, protected by British eccentric

indicators.note: protected by puts the say word inside the next pieces

parts.note: a nut is a crazy, eccentric person
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: A tree is guarded by an odd Briton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like an example marker; here it is a verb, the word protected by British and eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: The butternut is a North American walnut tree.

clue.text: Boundless competition involving people from apartments?

definitions.meaning: a horse race with no fences to leap
a whimsical race of people who live in flats

explanation.surface: An unlimited contest involving people who live in flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundless' means without jumps, not unlimited.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat race is run on level ground without hurdles; flat dwellers might be called a flat race.

clue.text: Stop using program directly available from computers etc

parts.note: ex means sold direct from, as in 'ex works'
IT is information technology, computers and the like

explanation.surface: A command to leave software is supplied straight from the machines.
explanation.walkthrough: EX as in 'ex works' or 'ex stock': straight from the source.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to quit or close a computer program.

clue.text: A form of rate-capping on the way

definitions.text: A form of rate-capping on the way

parts.words: A form of rate-capping on the way
parts.note: rate-capping was a British policy limiting local council taxes; read literally it is a cap on speed, imposed on the road

explanation.surface: A council tax limit is about to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: Rate-capping was a 1980s British cap on what local councils could charge; 'on the way' seems to mean coming soon but means on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal maximum on how fast traffic may go puts a ceiling on driving rate along a road.

clue.text: Old woodland revellers — mum gives up time for one

indicators.note: gives up one letter for another, a swap in the quiet word

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Mother quits her time for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; it is SILENT, whose T is swapped for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sileni were drunken woodland spirits, companions of Bacchus, in Greek myth.

clue.text: Waffle making teacher rage

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
the ton means the height of fashion, the current rage

explanation.surface: A breakfast item gets a teacher furious.
explanation.walkthrough: TON is an old word for fashion, the vogue; 'all the rage' means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for talking at length about little, to prattle.

clue.text: Concerning addiction — it's eliminated here

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: eliminated says the word it is removed from the habit

parts.note: a habit is an addiction

explanation.surface: Notes about addiction: the place where it is stamped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's eliminated' drops IT from HABIT; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is a treatment centre where dependence on drugs or drink is cured.

clue.text: Leading pairs of students oddly get for the bulk of the course

indicators.note: leading pairs asks for the opening two letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Odd students take the front positions for most of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like an anagram signal; it is only fodder for the first-pairs rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food, the kind that bulks out a meal course.

clue.text: Repetitious exercises are boring

definitions.meaning: practice by repetition, as soldiers do on parade
making holes, as with a power tool

explanation.surface: Doing the same exercises again and again is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means tedious in the surface; it is making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill is repeated practice, and drilling is making a hole.

clue.text: Make electronic copy of science article

parts.note: Sc is the abbreviation for science, as in BSc
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Digitising a scientific paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan something is to digitise it with a scanner, producing an image file.

clue.text: Throw up to the sky? Not half

annotationWithheld.why: 'Throw up to the sky? Not half (5)': the only parse is HEAVEN (the sky) losing its last letter, with 'Not half' meaning 'not quite whole'; one letter of six is not a half, so no halving fits and the check reads 'Not half' as one
annotationWithheld.clue: Throw up to the sky? Not half

clue.text: Initial food production total I can change

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to vary a running total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges TOTALICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactation is milk production, a baby's first nourishment.

clue.text: Unable to get up, ordered to swallow drug given by doctor

indicators.note: to swallow means the ordered word takes the next pieces inside it

parts.note: bidden means commanded or ordered

indicators.note: given by places the doctor right after the drug

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A patient is told to take medicine prescribed by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given by' sets the doctor straight after the drug, and that pair is what is swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined to bed by illness or age cannot rise from it.

clue.text: Foreign port — consume about one litre

indicators.note: about says the eating word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: to consume food is to eat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Drinking about a litre in an overseas harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts I and L inside EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eilat is Israel's port at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.
